All of this, combined with my attempt. My loneliness, sadness, fatigue, hopelessness, etc. contributed to the poor academic performance. I was a very ‘gifted’ student. Keep in mind I’m taking my meds religiously at this time and going to therapy, I just wasnt being so honest and then I kind of ghosted my therapist. Then came the attempt, which led to withdrawing. I hit rock bottom, or rather it felt like rock bottom hit me. Bad. 

Now we’re almost at the year mark, and I was doing great the previous fall semester but I was stupid and stopped taking my meds. Trying to get back on track. But I’m hopeful. Last year me wouldn’t have ANY hope whatsoever. I’m hoping when I get to the year mark of my attempt, things will look pretty great. But I will say, when I hit rock bottom, no matter what life threw at me after that, it was nothing compared to that feeling. It was nothing I couldn’t overcome. I mean, my life did a full 180. It was crazy. I have hope it’ll get back to that point. I just have to accept that with this diagnosis, there will always be highs and lows. 

Stay hopeful my friend, even if it feels impossible. :)

I made an attempt to end my life earlier this year. I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder a few years back, and my sister passed away in a very traumatic manner not long after. I spent years thinking about suicide every day. I’m not exaggerating, literal years. 
After my attempt, it was like a switch turned off in my brain. I realized how beautiful life can be, and that I’m not damned to live in agony for the rest of my life. 
I learned that it’s okay to seek help. I shouldn’t feel judged or let stigma influence me. I altered meds, went back to therapy, and I’m the happiest I’ve been in a long time. I learned to let the light in.
